gpt_pro_web_attempt.details: tool_search was queried for Browser/iab ChatGPT Pro control, but the exposed callable tools did not include an in-app Browser/iab route for ChatGPT.com Pro in this session.

diagnosis: The immediate failure mode is monitor-to-held-out transfer, not simply insufficient objective pressure.
Run7 and run8 looked strong on monitor verification but transferred worse than run6 on held-out verification.

Before another objective, capacity change, or score transform, the smallest useful next slice is to audit whether a monitor-only robust checkpoint-selection rule from the run6 base could reduce monitor overfit.
If existing artifacts cannot evaluate more than the already selected run6 checkpoint, the next slice should report that insufficiency rather than infer a paid recipe.

selected_no_brev_preflight.summary: Run a local CPU/no-training run6 monitor/checkpoint-selection stability preflight using existing run6 receipts/logs/artifacts only.
candidate_rules: current max monitor verification recall selector
earliest epoch within epsilon of max monitor verification recall
5-epoch smoothed or median monitor selector if per-epoch monitor history is available
class-bootstrap lower-confidence-bound selector on monitor verification recall if per-class monitor recalls are available
nearby-epoch stability selector if intermediate run6 artifacts exist
required_outputs: artifact sufficiency inventory for run6 logs, per-epoch metrics, and any available checkpoint/logit artifacts
reproduction of current run6 held-out verification recall@FAR10 0.8038559556786704 within tolerance
held-out test metrics reported only after selector definitions are fixed
per-class recall and positive-margin regression comparison versus current run6
pass_criteria: No Brev lifecycle command is run.
No optimizer step or backward pass occurs.
No checkpoint, model export, or browser/runtime artifact is written or promoted.
No raw learner video is uploaded.
No pretrained runtime dependency is introduced.
No raw test-mined pairs are used as training supervision.
Local replay reproduces run6 held-out verification recall@FAR10 0.8038559556786704 within established tolerance.
Every candidate selector is defined using monitor data only before held-out test reporting.
A pre-registered robust selector improves held-out verification recall@FAR10 by at least 0.005 absolute over current run6, or the slice records fail-closed with no paid recipe.
The selected rule does not create broad run7/run8-like class damage: fewer than 15 classes regress by more than 0.05 recall and no dominant positive-margin damage signature.
Top-5 does not drop more than about 0.02 absolute versus run6 unless verification gain is larger and class damage remains limited.
fail_criteria: Required run6 artifacts are insufficient to evaluate more than the already-selected checkpoint.
Local replay cannot reproduce run6 metrics within tolerance.
Robust monitor-only selectors do not improve held-out verification recall.
Any apparent improvement depends on using held-out test results to choose the selector.
The selector creates broad per-class recall or positive-margin regressions.
The slice attempts training, optimizer/backward steps, checkpoint writing, export, browser promotion, Brev lifecycle, or raw test-mined supervision.

why_other_preflights_lower_priority: Post-hoc score transforms are lower priority because the audit shows positive-margin/ranking damage rather than a simple threshold-calibration issue; flexible transforms risk monitor overfit.
Class or teacher coverage audits remain useful later for repeated weak words, but they do not directly address the demonstrated monitor-to-test selection failure.
Objective-simulation audits for positive margins are directionally relevant, but choosing another objective before validating selection stability risks repeating run7/run8.
T=40/cache/capacity is lower priority because run8 improved top-1 while hurting verification, so more classification capacity could again miss the primary metric.

future_paid_recipe.reason: The local preflight has not yet proven a safer checkpoint-selection rule or future objective; launching a paid recipe now risks repeating monitor-overfit.
future_paid_recipe.only_after_preflight_passes: A future run6-like objective/envelope with improved monitor/checkpoint-selection discipline may become reasonable only after the local preflight passes, Brev auth is recovered, and a future receipt records the exact bounded compute envelope.

brev_auth_prerequisite.reason: Run8 teardown lost Brev CLI API visibility; future compute must first recover auth and verify worker state.

next_action.summary: Use existing run6 artifacts only to test monitor-only robust checkpoint-selection rules before any paid run or new objective is selected.
